findings.evidence: Input redirection precedes stderr suppression in tr invocation. If the pattern file disappears or loses readability after the readable-file check and before open, Bash emits the private path before fail() emits neutral text. Invented-data repro: safe staged blob passes with exit 0; mktemp shim removes invented pattern then delegates /usr/bin/mktemp; hook exits 2 but full invented pattern path appears in stderr. D4 forbids private-path logging. Redirect stderr before opening private input (or equivalently suppress the whole command) and retain a race-at-open regression. This is path disclosure, not demonstrated term-content disclosure.

The [[ $(cat control) == 1 ]] expression tests only stdout and discards cat status. Invented-data repro: safe control exits 0; a cat shim delegates /bin/cat and then exits 19; hook still exits 0 with clean scanned-count output. D4 requires explicit external status classification and exit 2 on operational/self-control failure. Capture the read result/status separately and regress a partial-output nonzero reader; do not merely test a reader that emits nothing.
